items.context: @mikewmunz (6.289 seguidores), en inglés: «The talk for 2.5 years has been Bitcoin bear markets would not see the 70%+ drawdowns from peak to trough going forward. The anticipated cycle was 30%-50% drawdown. We've extended a little further to mid 50% but it's right in line with the speculation. It is right on track» (cita otro post). Cuenta mediana, 7 likes y 0 respuestas: espacio libre y tema exacto de caídas y ciclos (Cycle Clock: profundidad y días de recuperación).
items.suggested_text:
The shrinking-drawdown idea has a real basis: 2011 was -92.7%, 2013 -84.5%, then roughly -84% in 2018 and -77% in 2022. Each cycle a bit shallower, as more supply sits with holders who don't sell into panic and liquidity deepens.

But depth is only half of a drawdown. The 2011 top took 622 days to reclaim, the 2013 one 1,177. A shallower fall can still be a long one, and time underwater tends to wear people down more than the percentage does.

Mid-50% fits the trend line. Whether this cycle also compresses the recovery time, or only the depth, is the part the chart can't show yet.
